audit_items.title: Verify Merkle Proof Construction: Does get_data_column_sidecars_from_block (SG-004/validator) use correct generalized index?

state_anomalies.description: The generalized index is hardcoded as 'kzgPosition = 11' (line 11). This value should be fork-specific. For Fulu fork BeaconBlockBody, the blob_kzg_commitments field position may have changed due to struct modifications.

No validation that the generalized index (kzgPosition) is correct for the current fork. If the BeaconBlockBody structure changed in Fulu fork, using the wrong index causes all proofs to fail verification.
state_anomalies.impact: All data column sidecars would fail verification if the generalized index is incorrect for Fulu fork

phase1_result.fork_awareness: NONE - hardcoded constant used across all forks

path_conditions: sidecar.SignedBlockHeader != nil AND sidecar.SignedBlockHeader.Header != nil -> compute trie
trie.VerifyMerkleProof(root, hashTreeRoot, 11, proof) -> CRITICAL: index 11 hardcoded
reachable_states: ErrInvalidInclusionProof if Merkle proof verification fails with generalized index 11

phase3_result.invariant: ∀ sidecar ∈ DataColumnSidecars: VerifyMerkleProof(BodyRoot, KZGCommitmentsRoot, GeneralizedIndex, InclusionProof) = true
phase3_result.violation_scenario: IF GeneralizedIndex (kzgPosition=11) != CORRECT_INDEX_FOR_FULU_FORK THEN all proofs fail verification
phase3_result.severity_justification: CRITICAL - incorrect generalized index breaks all data column sidecar verification on P2P network
phase3_result.consensus_impact: HIGH - nodes with wrong index reject all sidecars; nodes with correct index accept them -> network partition
phase3_result.recommended_fix: 1. Review Fulu fork BeaconBlockBody specification to confirm blob_kzg_commitments generalized index. 2. Add fork-aware generalized index selection. 3. Add test to verify index correctness against spec test vectors.

audit_items.title: Verify Subnet Mapping: Is each sidecar published to correct gossip subnet?

phase1_result.determinism: DETERMINISTIC given same DataColumnSidecarSubnetCount config value
phase1_result.cross_client_risk: HIGH if config values differ between clients

symbolic_execution.consistency_check: Same formula used across all Ethereum clients?

phase2_result.vulnerability_likelihood: MEDIUM - depends on config consistency across implementations

phase3_result.violation_scenario: IF DataColumnSidecarSubnetCount differs between client implementations THEN subnet mapping is inconsistent
phase3_result.severity_justification: HIGH - inconsistent subnet mapping fragments data availability network

phase1_result.dependency_analysis: Prysm uses github.com/crate-crypto/go-kzg-4844 or similar library for KZG operations

phase2_result.trust_assumption: KZG library correctly validates field elements
phase2_result.recommendation: Verify that the KZG library rejects values >= BLS_MODULUS. This should be tested at the integration level.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Can proofs be reused across different cells or commitments?

code_scope.excerpt: verified, err := kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitments, indices, cells, proofs)

phase1_result.proof_binding: Proofs are verified against specific (commitment, index, cell) tuples
phase1_result.fiat_shamir_challenge: KZG verification includes all components in pairing equation
phase1_result.reuse_prevention: Cryptographic binding - proof valid for exactly one (commitment, index, cell) triple

phase2_result.attack_scenario: Attacker takes valid (C1, idx1, cell1, proof1) and attempts to use proof1 with (C2, idx2, cell2)
phase2_result.verification_result: Batch verification will fail because pairing equation e(proof, G2) != e(commitment + challenge*H(idx), cell*G1)
phase2_result.cryptographic_guarantee: Fiat-Shamir challenge ensures proof is bound to specific (commitment, index, cell)

phase3_result.invariant: ∀ proof P: P is valid for exactly one (commitment, index, cell) triple
phase3_result.violation_scenario: IF proof can be reused THEN cryptographic binding is broken (catastrophic KZG failure)
phase3_result.severity_justification: CRITICAL - proof reuse would allow false data availability claims
phase3_result.cryptographic_soundness: ASSUMED SOUND - KZG proof binding is fundamental property
phase3_result.recommended_action: Add test attempting proof reuse to confirm rejection

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are mutually inconsistent recovery cells detected?

code_scope.excerpt: Recovery logic found in target_workspace/beacon-chain/core/peerdas/reconstruction.go. Post-recovery verification should occur.

phase1_result.recovery_process: Reed-Solomon erasure coding recovery from partial cells
phase1_result.inconsistency_detection: Requires post-recovery verification to detect inconsistent inputs
phase1_result.verification_requirement: Recovered cells MUST be verified against commitments before acceptance

phase2_result.attack_scenario: Attacker provides individually valid but mutually inconsistent cells from different polynomials
phase2_result.detection_mechanism: Post-recovery KZG verification will fail if recovered cells don't match original commitment

phase3_result.violation_scenario: IF inconsistent cells provided AND no post-recovery verification THEN incorrect data accepted
phase3_result.severity_justification: CRITICAL - accepting incorrect recovered data breaks data availability guarantees
phase3_result.verification_status: REQUIRES_CODE_REVIEW of reconstruction.go to confirm post-recovery verification
phase3_result.recommended_action: 1. Review reconstruction.go for post-recovery verification. 2. Add test with inconsistent cells to confirm rejection.
